quizzes.title: Corridors and Connectivity with Russia
quizzes.passage:
India and Russia treat transport links as a practical part of their wider partnership. The 23rd Annual Summit, held in New Delhi, discussed several corridors that could make the movement of goods between the two countries easier. The most prominent proposal is the Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor, a sea route linking the Indian port of Chennai with the Russian port of Vladivostok. Its stated purpose is to carry cargo and reduce the time needed to reach Russia compared with the existing route between the two ports.

A second channel is the International North-South Transport Corridor, a transport network that includes India, Russia and other member states. Both corridors appear in the summit's connectivity agenda, which also covers Russia's Far East and the Arctic.

Cooperation in the Far East and the Arctic is guided by a separate programme, which lists several sectors for joint work. These sectors include mining, pharmaceuticals and manpower. The summit also addressed trade more generally, with a comprehensive programme meant to diversify ties beyond defence and energy.

The partnership itself has a long history. India and Russia have a treaty of peace and friendship, and in 2010 their relationship was upgraded to a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. Transport planning sits alongside these political agreements, and the summit documents list connectivity among its major outcomes.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed among the key areas of India-Russia Far East and Arctic cooperation?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists agriculture and mining, manpower and pharmaceuticals, and diamonds and shipping as the key Far East and Arctic areas.

questions.q: Which three countries set up the International North-South Transport Corridor in 2000?
questions.explanation: The INSTC was established in 2000 in St Petersburg by Iran, Russia and India.

questions.q: Through which of the following water bodies does the proposed Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor pass?
questions.explanation: The proposed sea route passes through the Sea of Japan, the South China Sea and the Malacca Strait.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The International North-South Transport Corridor was set up to promote transportation cooperation among its member states.
Reason (R): The INSTC is a multi-modal transportation route.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the multi-modal nature of the route does not explain the aim of promoting cooperation.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Northern Sea Route   ->   A. Arctic shipping
II. Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor   ->   B. Proposed sea route
III. Arctic Council   ->   C. India is an Observer
IV. India-Russia Far East Cooperation Programme   ->   D. Covers 2024-2029
questions.explanation: Each item in List I matches its own description in List II: Northern Sea Route for Arctic shipping, the proposed sea route, India as Arctic Council observer, and the 2024-2029 programme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the connectivity measures discussed at the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit:
I. The proposed Chennai-Vladivostok corridor is expected to save up to 16 days of transport time.
II. The International North-South Transport Corridor was established in 2000.
III. India is a full member of the Arctic Council.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because India is only an Observer in the Arctic Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the connectivity corridors discussed at the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit:
I. The proposed Chennai-Vladivostok route passes through the South China Sea.
II. The International North-South Transport Corridor was established in St Petersburg.
III. The India-Russia Far East Cooperation Programme covers the period 2010-2020.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because the Far East programme covers 2024-2029.

questions.q: In which year was the International North-South Transport Corridor established? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the INSTC was established in 2000.

questions.q: By how many days can the proposed Chennai-Vladivostok Maritime Corridor save transport time? (days, up to)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the time saving of the proposed corridor as up to 16 days.

quizzes.title: Diplomacy, Honours and Dialogue
quizzes.passage:
India and Russia have a long diplomatic history, and the 23rd Annual Summit in New Delhi showed how both governments view the partnership. The meeting marked 25 years of strategic partnership, and its outcomes covered economic, defence, energy and migration topics. The summit also marked Russia's President's first visit to India in four years.

Security was another focus of the discussions. Both sides condemned attacks that had taken place in their countries. The two governments also discussed their cooperation in international forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS and SCO.

Honours also featured in the summit's record. Russia's highest national award was conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his contribution to fostering India-Russia ties. The award was presented during the visit, and it recognised the work done to strengthen bilateral relations.

Dialogue between the two countries also takes other forms. A platform for enhancing the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership, which was upgraded in 2010, involves government bodies and research institutions. The summit documents describe cooperation in areas such as nuclear energy and defence, and they mention regular defence exercises as well. The defence agenda also includes joint research and development, co-production under Make in India, and military technology transfer.

questions.q: Which Tsar established the Order of St Andrew the Apostle in 1698?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the Order was established by Tsar Peter the Great in 1698.

questions.q: Which event is linked to the abolition of the Order of St Andrew the Apostle in 1918?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Order was abolished in 1918 following the Russian Revolution, which overthrew the Tsarist regime.

questions.q: Which ministry organised the Ganga-Volga Dialogue in collaboration with a research foundation?
questions.explanation: The Ganga-Volga Dialogue was organised by the Ministry of External Affairs with the Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Russia supports India's permanent membership of a reformed and expanded UN Security Council.
Reason (R): Both parties called for strict action against all UN-listed terrorist organisations.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the call for action against terrorist groups does not explain Russia's support for India's Security Council seat.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Order of St Andrew the Apostle   ->   A. Reinstated in 1998
II. Ganga-Volga Dialogue   ->   B. Conceptualised during the 2018 summit
III. Emblem of the Order of St Andrew   ->   C. Double-headed eagle
IV. Pahalgam attack (2025)   ->   D. Denounced by both parties
questions.explanation: The Order was reinstated in 1998, the Ganga-Volga Dialogue was conceptualised in 2018, the emblem is a double-headed eagle, and both parties denounced the Pahalgam attack.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the outcomes linked to the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit:
I. The Treaty of Peace and Friendship between India and Russia was signed in 1971.
II. The Ganga-Volga Dialogue is organised by the Ministry of Defence.
III. Both parties called for a Zero-Tolerance Policy grounded in international law.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because the Ministry of External Affairs organises the Ganga-Volga Dialogue.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the honours and dialogues linked to the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit:
I. The Ganga-Volga Dialogue was conceptualised during the 2018 India-Russia summit.
II. The Order of St Andrew the Apostle features a double-headed eagle emblem.
III. The Order of St Andrew the Apostle was reinstated in 1918.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because the Order was reinstated in 1998.
